newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-UNBEATEN BLUES SAIL TO SUPER 12 FINAL.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-UNBEATEN BLUES SAIL TO SUPER 12 FINAL.

text.p: The Auckland Blues maintained their incredible unbeaten run in this year's Super 12 rugby by trouncing the Natal Sharks 55-36 in Saturday's semifinal at Auckland's Eden Park.

A clinical, blistering first half performance saw the defending champions 33-5 clear at halftime. Although Natal produced a stirring late fightback, the Blues were always cruising to victory and a home final next weekend.

Auckland ran in eight tries, six of them converted by fullback Adrian Cashmore, and their dominance was such that by the end of the game they had conceded six tries but still got home with room to spare.
Natal coach Ian McIntosh was gracious in defeat.
Asked if he envisaged Auckland being beaten in the final -- by either ACT of the Wellington Hurricanes -- at Eden Park, he replied: "Beaten here? Not in your lifetime".
The Blues were irresistible in the first half, running riot after Natal scored in the opening minutes through winger Shaun Payne, who finished with two tries along with wing colleague Joos Joubert.

A 70 metre sideline run in the sixth minute by winger Joeli Vidiri put the Blues in front 7-5 after Cashmore's conversion; No 8 Zinzan Brooke crossed from a tapped penalty and Vidiri scored his second try to take the score to 21-5.

Midway through the half the Auckland loose-forwards combined to send openside flanker Mark Carter galloping under the posts, and on halftime fly-half Carlos Spencer and centre Lee Stensness dribbled the ball all the way from a quick 22 dropout for Spencer to dot down.

Two tries to centre Eroni Clarke in the first 15 minutes of the second half had the Blues home and dry, although Natal rallied superbly to restore a large measure of dented pride with five tries of their own.
The Sharks were brilliant in the final quarter as Payne, Joubert, fly-half Henry Honiball and replacement back Errol Stewart all went over in the final quarter.
Blues coach Graham Henry played dpwn his side's achievements.
"We do have concerns with the way we have allowed teams like the ACT and then Wellington and today Natal to come back in the second half," he said.
"We played as well as we have this season in the first half but the second half was a concern."
The last word on the match was left to Natal coach McIntosh.
"They have probably the best defensive loose-forwards in world provincial rugby," McIntosh said.

Auckland Blues: 15-Adrian Cashmore; 14-Joeli Vidiri, 13-Eroni Clarke, 12-Lee Stensness, 11-Brian Lima; 10-Carlos Spencer, 9-Ofisa Tonu'u; 8-Zinzan Brooke (captain); 7-Mark Carter, 6-Michael Jones, 5-Robin Brooke, 4-Leo Lafaiali'i; 3-Olo Brown, 2-Sean Fitzpatrick, 1-Craig Dowd.

Natal Sharks: 15-Andre Joubert; 14-Joos Joubert, 13-Jeremy Thomson, 12-Pieter Muller, 11-Shaun Payne; 10-Henry Honiball, 9- Kevin Putt; 8-Gary Teichmann (captain); 7-Wayne Fyvie, 6-Wickus van Heerden, 5-Wayne Boardman, 4-John Slade; 3-Adrian Garvey, 2- John Allan, 1-Rob Kempson.
